bihar_raw_news.content: Museum Ranking 2026: Bihar museum secures top position in Asia, ranks 9th globally The ranking identifies 10 museums in Asia, with institutions from Japan, Malaysia, South Korea, Indonesia and India featuring on the list Join Our WhatsApp Channel Business Today Desk Updated Oct 28, 2026 3:00 AM IST Bihar Museum is the only Indian institution featured among the 100 museums selected worldwide The Bihar Museum in Patna has earned international recognition after securing the ninth position in the World’s 100 Best Museums 2026 list published by travel platform Worth a Journey. The museum has also been ranked the best in Asia, placing Bihar’s rich historical and cultural heritage in the global spotlight. Advertisement According to the ranking, Bihar Museum is the only Indian institution featured among the 100 museums selected worldwide. Its ninth-place finish puts it among some of the world’s most prominent cultural institutions, highlighting its role in preserving and showcasing India’s heritage. Here is why tourists are paying ₹1.06 lakh to visit this ‘Ghost Island Bihar museum among global leaders The 2026 list features museums dedicated to art, history, science, technology and open-air collections across different continents. Mexico City’s Museo Nacional de Antropología secured the first position, followed by Spain’s Museo del Prado in second place and Denmark’s Louisiana Museum of Modern Art in third. The State Hermitage Museum in Russia and Vienna’s Kunsthistorisches Museum also featured among the top 10 institutions. Bihar Museum’s inclusion in this group marks a significant achievement for India’s museum and cultural tourism sector. Advertisement The ranking identifies 10 museums in Asia, with institutions from Japan, Malaysia, South Korea, Indonesia and India featuring on the list. Bihar Museum emerged as the continent’s highest-ranked institution, ahead of other prominent Asian museums. Showcasing Bihar’s rich cultural heritage Established in Patna, Bihar Museum is a modern state museum that traces the region’s history from the Stone Age to contemporary times. Its collection includes ancient sculptures, coins, manuscripts, archaeological artefacts and regional folk art. The museum’s galleries are arranged chronologically, helping visitors understand Bihar’s historical development and cultural evolution. Its spacious premises, open courtyards and landscaped lawns complement the exhibitions. national_raw_news.title: Home Ministry directs respective state govts to take precautionary measures in view of Cyclone Ar...
national_raw_news.content: The Ministry of Home Affairs has directed State Governments to keep a close watch, monitor the situation in their areas regularly and take appropriate precautionary measures in view of Cyclone Arnab. The Ministry has also asked the States to keep it informed of any developments in this regard at the Integrated Control Room for Emergency Response on telephone numbers 011-23438252, 011-23438253 and 011-23438254. In an advisory, the Ministry has suggested evacuating people living in coastal areas to safer places and complete suspension of fishing operations. The Ministry has issued advisory to Chief Secretaries of West Bengal, Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nādu, Puducherry, Telangana, Sikkim, Jharkhand, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh and Andaman and Nicobar. The Ministry has urged the residents of affected areas to remain indoors and avoid staying in vulnerable structures. It called for judicious regulation of rail and road traffic and urged people to follow traffic advisories issued by the authorities. People have also been advised to avoid areas that are prone to frequent waterlogging and movement in motorboats and small ships has been declared unsafe. The Ministry asked fisheries departments and fishing harbour authorities to alert fishermen and monitor subsequent marine warnings issued by the India Meteorological Department. Fishermen have been advised to plan their activities in accordance with the latest area-specific advisories till tomorrow. Maritime authorities have been asked to review communication systems, vessel tracking and search and rescue preparedness, particularly for vessels operating in areas likely to be affected.

national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi today stated that India must innovate and lead the world in shaping the technologies of tomorrow. Speaking at the Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave in New Delhi, Mr Modi said India must embrace the technologies of the future, innovate boldly and lead the world in creating them. He stressed that a Viksit Bharat will be built on strong foundations of scientific research, discoveries and the spirit of innovation. Mr Modi said India aims to achieve self-reliance and build strength in critical technologies. He highlighted that the India of the 21st Century is moving ahead with a new mindset and new found confidence. He stated that the goal is to create new technology for India, for the world, for today, and for the days to come. Prime Minister Modi visited different sections of the exhibition and interacted with people. The exhibition includes around 150 deep-tech startup stalls, which will highlight technological developments and their potential applications across sectors. The three-day Conclave brings together leading scientists, researchers, academicians, policymakers, industry leaders, startups and international experts to deliberate on emerging technologies and India’s science, technology and innovation priorities. The deliberations will span 12 thematic areas, including artificial intelligence, biotechnology, advanced materials, manufacturing, healthcare, energy, climate and ocean sciences. Discussions will focus on research priorities, national capabilities and translating scientific advances into practical applications.

national_raw_news.title: India set to become major exporter to China and ASEAN: Piyush Goyal 5 hours ago 94
national_raw_news.content: Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal has said, India is open to Chinese suppliers to meet its growing import needs, but will take action through established legal procedures if any unfair pricing is detected. Mr Goyal stated this while talking to reporters in The Hague during his two-day official visit to the Netherlands. He expressed hope that India will emerge as a major exporter to China and the ASEAN region in the coming years. He stressed that India believes in free and fair trade with all countries. The Commerce and Industry Ministry said India also wants greater access to international markets for its goods and services on a reciprocal basis. He expressed confidence that India would become a major exporter to China and Southeast Asian countries in the years ahead. His remarks come amid a significant rise in bilateral trade between India and China. According to the Commerce Ministry, bilateral trade between the two countries rose by around 29 per cent to 91.76 billion US dollars during April to September of the current financial year, making China India’s largest trading partner in the first half of 2026-27. Meanwhile, Mr Goyal said India would work to address the impact of China’s new export controls on key machinery, including tunnel boring machines

national_raw_news.title: Cyclone Arnab to hit Andhra coast tomorrow forenoon as very severe storm, says IMD 3 hours ago 42
national_raw_news.content: Cyclone Arnab will hit Bapatla and Visakhapatnam in Andhra Pradesh, close to Yanam, as a very severe cyclonic storm tomorrow forenoon. Talking exclusively to Akashvani, Director General of India Meteorological Department (IMD) Dr. Mrutyunjay Mohapatra said that during landfall activity, the cyclone will have maximum sustained wind upto 125 to 150 kilometres per hour. Dr. Mohapatra has cautioned people of destructive winds, heavy rainfall and coastal flooding. He noted that the cyclone is likely to damage houses, trees, power lines and standing crops. The DG IMD has advised people in vulnerable low-lying areas to evacuate and urged them to remain in safe places till tomorrow afternoon. He said that storm surge of 2.5 meter height above astronomical tide may inundate low-lying coastal areas, particularly around Kakinada during the time of landfall. Meanwhile, IMD has issued a red colour warning for extremely heavy rainfall over Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Odisha and Chhattisgarh tomorrow. Heavy to very heavy weather is likely to prevail over Telangana and Vidarbha tomorrow. Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Assam, Meghalaya, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram, Tripura, East Madhya Pradesh, Gangetic West Bengal and Jharkhand will witness heavy rainfall for next two day. The Met Department has forecast thunderstorms accompanied with lightning and gusty winds over Bihar, Haryana, Chandigarh, Delhi, Maharashtra and East Uttar Pradesh for next two to three days. Similar conditions are likely to prevail over Interior Karnataka, Kerala, Mahe and Rayalaseema.

national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi today held a bilateral meeting with the Acting Head of State of the Principality of Liechtenstein, Hereditary Prince Alois, at Hyderabad House in New Delhi. Both the leaders discussed cooperation in various areas, including trade and investment, science, technology and innovation and people-to-people exchanges. They also exchanged views on regional and global developments. Prince Alois was accorded a ceremonial reception at the forecourt of Rashtrapati Bhavan this morning. President Droupadi Murmu and Prime Minister Narendra Modi welcomed him. In a media statement, Prince Alois said that the visit bears testimony to the importance that Liechtenstein attaches to the relationship with India. He said that the conclusion of the trade and economic partnership agreement, TEPA, with India, which entered into force a year ago, marked a significant milestone in this regard. He further said that Liechtenstein is determined to build on this momentum and strengthen ties with India even further. Prince Alois also expressed gratitude to Prime Minister Narendra Modi for the invitation. Prince Alois and his spouse, Princess Sophie, also paid homage to Mahatma Gandhi at Raj Ghat in New Delhi. He will also meet President Droupadi Murmu at Rashtrapati Bhavan this evening, who will also host an official banquet in the honour of the visiting dignitary. The acting Head of State of the Principality of Liechtenstein arrived in New Delhi yesterday from Vadodara. Union Minister Jayant Singh received him at the airport. He was accompanied by his spouse, Princess Sophie and a high-level official, as well as a business delegation comprising top industry leaders. This is the second visit of Prince Alois to India in 2026. He earlier visited New Delhi in February this year to attend the AI Impact Summit. He had previously visited India in 2010 and 2018. Ministry of External Affairs said the visit is expected to provide further impetus to the growing engagement between India and Liechtenstein, particularly since operationalization of the India-EFTA Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement last year. The visit will provide an opportunity to further deepen the friendly ties between India and Liechtenstein and build partnerships in new areas of mutual interest.

national_raw_news.title: Polling underway in Israel to elect new Parliament
national_raw_news.content: Polling is underway across Israel, with voters choosing representatives to the country’s 120-member Knesset. With 7.3 million eligible voters and 36 parties contesting the election, the outcome will determine the balance of power in parliament. Voting will end at 10 pm local time tonight. The election comes amid intense debate over national security, the October 7, 2023, Hamas attacks, military service and the country’s future political direction. The election is widely viewed as a test of Netanyahu’s leadership, with opposition figures, including former military chief Gadi Eisenkot and former prime minister Naftali Bennett, seeking to challenge his right-wing coalition. Israel follows a nationwide proportional representation system in which the entire country constitutes a single electoral constituency. Political parties must secure at least 3.25% of the national vote to enter the Knesset. Netanyahu, leader of the right-wing Likud party, has served as prime minister for nearly 19 years across three separate periods since 1996. Former Israel Defence Forces chief of staff Gadi Eisenkot, who leads the centrist Yashar party, has emerged as one of Netanyahu’s principal challengers. Former prime minister Naftali Bennett is leading the B’Yachad electoral alliance, which includes former prime minister Yair Lapid’s Yesh Atid party. Other significant political players include Yair Golan’s left-leaning Democrats, Avigdor Liberman’s Yisrael Beiteinu and Arab-led parties such as Ra’am and the Joint List.

national_raw_news.title: 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum concludes with unanimous Joint Declaration
national_raw_news.content: The 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum concluded today with the adoption of the Joint Declaration unanimously. The Joint Declaration reflects the BRICS member nations’ commitment to further strengthening parliamentary cooperation and advancing their shared objectives under the four key themes – Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability. During the second and final day of the two-day Forum, Lok Sabha Speaker and Chairperson of the 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum Om Birla proposed the unanimous adoption of the Joint Declaration. After that, Mr Birla handed over the Chairship of the BRICS Forum for 2027 to China. Later, Mr Birla delivered his valedictory address at Central Hall of Samvidhan Sadan, in which he called for greater dialogue, trust and cooperation among nations to address global challenges. Mr. Birla said that despite differences in opinions, backgrounds and challenges, BRICS countries share a common commitment to human welfare, peace and prosperity. Mr. Birla emphasised the need to respect the sovereignty of every nation, resolve international disputes peacefully and ensure equitable development opportunities for all. The Lok Sabha Speaker said that during the two-day forum, the discussions focused not only on current challenges but also on exploring new avenues for future cooperation. Highlighting the prevailing global conflicts, regional instability and economic uncertainty, Mr. Birla stressed that dialogue and cooperation are more important than ever. He said India believes that lasting solutions to global problems can be achieved through dialogue rather than conflict, peace rather than war, and cooperation rather than competition. He added that global peace must guarantee security, dignity and justice, along with the promise of a better future for everyone, particularly the younger generation. Mr Birla said that through the joint declaration, the participating countries reaffirmed their commitment to the principles of the United Nations Charter, sovereign equality of nations, mutual respect, non-interference in internal affairs and the peaceful settlement of international disputes. He said, the declaration also strongly condemned all acts of terrorism and called for coordinated and concrete action against all terrorists and terrorist organisations. Emphasising the use of Artificial Intelligence, Mr. Birla said its application should be guided by the principles of ethics, transparency, accountability and human welfare. He stressed that technology should improve human life and its development must remain aligned with human values. Mr. Birla said the success of BRICS should not be limited to the progress of its member countries but should also have a positive impact on the wider global community. He emphasised that the aspirations of the Global South must receive due consideration in global decision-making processes. The 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum began yesterday with the theme Fostering Parliaments for People-Centric Development.

national_raw_news.title: 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum to conclude today in New Delhi
national_raw_news.content: The two-day 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum will conclude in New Delhi today. Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla, who is also the Chairperson of the Forum, will deliver the valedictory speech after the adoption of the joint statement. Thereafter, the presidency will be handed over to China. Vice President C P Radhakrishnan will host lunch in honour of the presiding officers and leaders of the delegation of Member and Partner Countries. The second and final day of the forum will begin with the fourth plenary on Sustainability: The role of parliaments in fostering a sustainable and inclusive future for our nations. The 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum began yesterday with the theme “Fostering Parliaments for People-Centric Development. Prime Minister Narendra Modi interacted with MPs from BRICS nations during the Forum. They exchanged perspectives on a wide range of issues. In his inaugural address, Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla called upon the Parliaments of BRICS member and partner countries to strengthen their collective resolve towards people-centric development, global peace, sustainability and international cooperation. Emphasizing the transformative potential of parliamentary engagement, he underscored the need to harness the collective wisdom of nations to address shared challenges, deepen mutual understanding and bring meaningful, positive change to the lives of citizens. Mr Birla also addressed the First Plenary Session of the Forum, which focused on the Critical Role of Parliaments in Strengthening Institutional Resilience for a Better Future. Addressing the Second Plenary Session focusing on Harnessing Parliaments for Promoting Human-centric Innovation in Artificial Intelligence and Digital Technologies, Mr Birla said, from Artificial Intelligence to Digital Transformation, the challenge is not merely to embrace emerging technologies but to ensure that they serve humanity, promote inclusive growth, expand equal opportunities and empower citizens. The third plenary was on Cooperation: Leveraging Parliamentary cooperation for a more representative global governance architecture. On the sidelines of the 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum 2026, Mr Birla today held bilateral meetings with the Speaker of the Federal National Council of the UAE, Mr Saqr Ghobash; Vice Chairman of the National People’s Congress of China, Mr Zheng Jianbang; and a member of the Praesidium of the Islamic Consultative Assembly of Iran, Mr Ahmed Naderi. During the meeting between Om Birla and the Speaker of the Federal National Council of the UAE, Saqr Ghobash, both sides reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthening the historic bonds of friendship between India and the UAE through enhanced parliamentary cooperation, regular dialogue and exchanges of parliamentary delegations. They also exchanged views on regional developments and underscored the importance of dialogue and diplomacy in promoting peace and stability. During the meeting between Om Birla and Vice Chairman of the National People’s Congress of China, Zheng Jianbang, the two leaders discussed strengthening India-China relations through parliamentary exchanges, regular dialogue and cooperation in areas such as education, healthcare and technology. Mr Birla emphasised that, as neighbours, these two countries have a shared responsibility to maintain peace and tranquillity along the border and resolve differences amicably through dialogue and mutual respect. During his meeting with the Member of the Praesidium of the Islamic Consultative Assembly of Iran, Ahmed Naderi, Mr Birla emphasised the importance of peace and stability in the region for the welfare of humanity and highlighted the role of parliamentary dialogue and bilateral engagements in advancing these shared objectives. The two sides also discussed taking forward Chabahar Port cooperation through joint efforts. Mr. Naderi expressed gratitude for the medicines, assistance and other support extended by India to Iran.

national_raw_news.title: EC defends SIR of electoral rolls before Supreme Court
national_raw_news.content: The Election Commission has defended its Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls before the Supreme Court, maintaining that the exercise was authorised by law and the relevant orders were approved unanimously by all three members of the Commission. Rejecting the allegations that Form 6 had been amended, the poll panel, in its 248-page response to the petition against the chief election commissioner (CEC), said that no changes were made to the statutory Form 6 used for voter registration. A bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant is scheduled to hear on Tuesday petitions against CEC Gyanesh Kumar and the decisions taken by the poll panel during the SIR. In a counter-affidavit, the poll body sought summary dismissal of the petitions and called the allegations misconceived, which rested on a single newspaper report. The affidavit, filed by Deputy Election Commissioner Bhanu Prakash Yeturu on behalf of the Commission said attempt to make aspersions against the Election Commission is unfortunate. It said the affidavit itself had been approved for filing by a unanimous decision of all three members of the Commission. The Affidavit said the three SIR orders were issued in accordance with decisions of the EC arrived at unanimously and taken in due compliance with Article 324 of the Constitution of India. The poll body said any suggestion, observation or query raised by a commissioner while a file is being processed does not constitute a decision of the Commission. On the Form 6 row, the EC said it unequivocally rejects the misleading contention that the statutory form had been changed. It added that Form 6 is an application through which an eligible person seeks inclusion in the electoral rolls According to the affidavit, the declaration attached during the SIR is a separate document provided by the SIR orders and “is not a part of Form 6. It said the declaration used in the Bihar SIR was later replaced in the subsequent orders so that applicants could give details of themselves and their parents or grandparents from the 2002-03 rolls and avoid submitting further documents once successfully mapped. The poll body also said that appeals filed in West Bengal against orders including electors in the rolls were filed by officers of the state chief electoral officer’s office acting as statutory authorities in line with the apex court’s orders, and that ” matters were not brought to the Commission. Questioning the maintainability of the pleas, the Commission said, in the eyes of law, a newspaper report is not treated as evidence of the facts it narrates. The Commission added that it has “neither released nor authorised the release of any internal note/ file to any news agency. Citing Article 324(5) of the Constitution, which protects the CEC from removal except in the manner of a Supreme Court judge, the EC said any prayer to restrain the CEC from functioning was not maintainable. It also rejected the petitioner’s contentions on electronic voting machines (EVMs). The EC said similar challenges had been rejected by the top court several times.

national_raw_news.title: PM Modi will inaugurate ESTIC 2026 today at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will inaugurate the Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave ESTIC 2026 today at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi. He will also address the gathering on the occasion. The three-day Conclave will bring together leading scientists, researchers, academicians, policymakers, industry leaders, startups and international experts to deliberate on emerging technologies and India’s science, technology and innovation priorities. The deliberations will span 12 thematic areas, including artificial intelligence, biotechnology, advanced materials, manufacturing, healthcare, energy, climate and ocean sciences. Discussions will focus on research priorities, national capabilities and translating scientific advances into practical applications. The Conclave will also feature an extensive technology and innovation exhibition showcasing indigenous scientific achievements and emerging technologies. It will include around 150 deep-tech startup stalls, which will highlight technological developments and their potential applications across sectors. The Conclave will also use thematic videos, technology demonstrations, documentaries, informational kiosks and augmented and virtual reality experiences to enhance engagement with scientific developments and their real-world applications. A new initiative, the Global Connect Networking Event, will bring together more than 300 invited participants from academia, research institutions and industry in India and abroad. It will provide a platform to explore international research partnerships, industry-academia collaboration and pathways for translating innovations from laboratories to markets.

national_raw_news.title: Cyclone Arnab moving towards Andhra Pradesh coast 51 mins ago 25
national_raw_news.content: Very Severe Cyclonic Storm Arnab over the Bay of Bengal is moving towards the Andhra Pradesh coast, with landfall expected tomorrow morning. Odisha is bracing for heavy to extremely heavy rainfall, particularly in its southern districts, as the storm approaches the eastern coastline. The State Government has intensified preparedness, while several train services have been cancelled or curtailed as a precaution. The weather has changed across southern and coastal Odisha under the influence of Very Severe Cyclonic Storm Arnab. Rain has started in southern Odisha, while coastal districts are witnessing cloudy skies as the cyclone moves closer to the eastern coast. The India Meteorological Department has warned of extremely heavy rainfall in Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Koraput and Malkangiri districts tomorrow. Heavy rain may trigger waterlogging, flash floods and landslides, while strong winds could damage power lines and disrupt communication. The State Government has intensified preparedness, with rescue teams on standby and ministers assigned to monitor vulnerable districts. Educational institutions in six districts will remain closed tomorrow and the day after tomorrow. Fishermen have been advised not to venture into the sea. Meanwhile, Railways have cancelled several services and curtailed others, including the Hirakhand Express, which will terminate at Rayagada instead of Jagdalpur. Passengers have been advised to check the latest train status before travelling.

national_raw_news.title: SIMBEX-2026: 33rd India-Singapore Maritime bilateral exercise concludes in Visakhapatnam
national_raw_news.content: SIMBEX-2026: 33rd India-Singapore Maritime bilateral exercise concludes in Visakhapatnam Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर SIMBEX-2026: 33rd India-Singapore Maritime bilateral exercise concludes in Visakhapatnam ANI | Updated: Oct 27, 2026 20:43 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 27 (ANI): The 33rd edition of the Singapore-India Maritime Bilateral Exercise (SIMBEX-2026), hosted by the Indian Navy at Visakhapatnam , concluded on October 26. According to the Ministry of Defence, the exercise further strengthened the longstanding maritime cooperation and operational engagement between the Indian Navy and the Republic of Singapore Navy (RSN). As part of the bilateral engagement, Colonel Bertram Ang, Fleet Commander of the RSN, called on RAdm Vishal Bishnoi, Flag Officer Commanding Eastern Fleet, and exchanged professional views on strengthening maritime cooperation between the two countries. The meeting provided an opportunity to discuss matters of mutual interest. SIMBEX-2026 was conducted in two phases. The Harbour Phase featured Subject Matter Expert Exchanges (SMEEs), cross-deck visits, professional interactions, sporting engagements and planning conferences, facilitating the exchange of operational knowledge and enhancing mutual understanding. The Sea Phase in the Bay of Bengal involved Maritime Interdiction Operations, Anti-Submarine Warfare (ASW), Anti-Air Warfare and Anti-Surface Warfare drills, seamanship evolutions and cross-deck flying operations, enhancing coordination and interoperability between the participating forces. The exercise witnessed the participation of RSN ship RSS Supreme, a Formidable-class stealth frigate with an embarked SH-70B helicopter, the ministry said. The Indian Navy was represented by the indigenously built stealth frigate INS Nilgiri, ASW corvette INS Kamorta and participating aviation assets, including P-8I and Dornier maritime patrol aircraft, Hawk Advanced Jet Trainers and MH-60R helicopters. SIMBEX has served as an important platform for strengthening bilateral maritime cooperation, operational interoperability and professional engagement between India and Singapore. The exercise also demonstrated the commitment of both nations to enhancing maritime security and promoting stability in the Indian Ocean Region (IOR). national_raw_news.title: Government of India Introduces Concessional Local Pass for National Highway Users Living ...
national_raw_news.content: Ministry of Road Transport & Highways Government of India Introduces Concessional Local Pass for National Highway Users Living Near Fee Plazas Eligible non-commercial vehicle owners residing within 20 km of a fee plaza can avail Concessional Local Pass for Rs. 1,500 per annum for fee plazas located outside municipal or local town area and Rs. 3,000 per annum for fee plazas situated within these limits depending on the location of the plaza Posted On: 27 OCT 2026 5:51PM by PIB Delhi In a major step to enhance ‘Ease of Living’ for citizens residing near National Highway Fee Plazas, the Government of India has introduced a ‘Concessional Local Pass’ for eligible non-commercial vehicle owners residing within 20 km of a National Highway fee plaza. The rule will come into effect from 01 st November 2026. The annual fee for the concessional Local Pass will be Rs.1,500 for fee plazas located outside municipal or local town area and Rs.3,000 for toll plazas situated within these limits. Under the new provision, eligible non-commercial vehicle owners with a valid and functional FASTag, residing within 20 km range can choose between the existing monthly pass and the concessional Local Pass for commuting through a specific fee plaza. The pass will be valid only for that fee plaza and will not be transferable to any other plazas. The concessional Local Pass will not be available on National Highways or Expressways where toll fee collection is based on a closed user-fee collection system. It will also not be issued where a service road or alternative road is available for use by commuters. The Annual Local Pass will be available at eligible Toll Plazas wef 01.11.2026. The Annual Local Pass will also be available through Rajmargyatra App wef 01.12.2026. The amendment has been notified through the National Highways Fee (Determination of Rates and Collection) (Fifth Amendment) Rules, 2026, under the powers conferred by the National Highways Act, 1956. The rates may be revised by the Central Government annually with revisions taking effect on 01 st April. With over 13 crore FASTags issued across the country, the new provision aims to provide an option for eligible residents living near toll plazas to make travel more economical and enhance Ease of Commuting for local residents. *** GDH/DS/HJ (Release ID: 2329077) Visitor Counter : 512 Read this release in: Urdu , हिन्दी , Marathi , Odia , Tamil Share -- words | -- min read Ministry of Road Transport & Highways Government of India Introduces Concessional Local Pass for National Highway Users Living Near Fee Plazas Eligible non-commercial vehicle owners residing within 20 km of a fee plaza can avail Concessional Local Pass for Rs. 1,500 per annum for fee plazas located outside municipal or local town area and Rs. 3,000 per annum for fee plazas situated within these limits depending on the location of the plaza Posted On: 27 OCT 2026 5:51PM by PIB Delhi In a major step to enhance ‘Ease of Living’ for citizens residing near National Highway...

national_raw_news.title: From Financial Hardship To Recovery: Mohan Lal's Journey
national_raw_news.content: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment From Financial Hardship To Recovery: Mohan Lal’s Journey Healthcare Support Through the NAMASTE Scheme and Ayushman Bharat–PM-JAY Posted On: 27 OCT 2026 6:43PM by PIB Delhi Access to timely healthcare makes a life-changing difference, particularly for workers facing economic hardship. The journey of Mohan Lal (name changed) , a 65-year-old waste picker from Jhansi, Uttar Pradesh, highlights how social protection and healthcare support can help vulnerable workers overcome serious medical challenges and move towards a healthier life. Coming from a financially disadvantaged family, Mohan Lal spent most of his life working as a contractual sanitation worker and waste picker, earning between Rs 101 and Rs 250 per day. His modest income was barely sufficient to meet his family’s basic needs, leaving little scope for savings or unexpected expenses. When he was diagnosed with a serious heart blockage requiring specialised treatment, the high cost of medical care became a major concern for him and his family. Enrolled under the Waste Pickers component of the National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE) Scheme, Mohan Lal received an Ayushman Card under Ayushman Bharat – Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY). This support enabled him to access treatment for his heart blockage at the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), New Delhi, on 8 May 2026, with the full cost of his medical treatment covered. Following successful treatment, Mohan Lal recovered and was able to return to work and resume supporting his family. Access to healthcare eased the financial burden associated with his medical emergency and helped him focus on recovery. The timely intervention also restored his confidence and provided renewed hope for the future. Mohan Lal’s journey demonstrates the importance of accessible healthcare and social protection for waste pickers and other vulnerable workers. His recovery reflects how welfare initiatives can help reduce barriers to essential medical treatment, safeguard dignity and strengthen family well-being. His story stands as an encouraging example of how timely support can help individuals move beyond difficult circumstances and look towards the future with renewed confidence. *** SS-149-TAR/KV/GA/RK (Release ID: 2329130) Visitor Counter : 95 Read this release in: Urdu , हिन्दी Share -- words | -- min read Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment From Financial Hardship To Recovery: Mohan Lal’s Journey Healthcare Support Through the NAMASTE Scheme and Ayushman Bharat–PM-JAY Posted On: 27 OCT 2026 6:43PM by PIB Delhi Access to timely healthcare makes a life-changing difference, particularly for workers facing economic hardship. national_raw_news.title: “India to bring further amendments to National Anti-Doping Act to introduce criminal ...
national_raw_news.content: “India to bring further amendments to National Anti-Doping Act to introduce criminal provisions”: Mansukh Mandaviya Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर “India to bring further amendments to National Anti-Doping Act to introduce criminal provisions”: Mansukh Mandaviya ANI | Updated: Oct 27, 2026 18:57 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 27 (ANI): Union Minister of Youth Affairs & Sports Mansukh Mandaviya chaired the third formal meeting of the COP10 Bureau and the fourth formal meeting of the Fund’s Approval Committee for 2026–27 under the UNESCO International Convention against Doping in Sport in New Delhi. According to a press release from the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, Mandaviya assured the Bureau of India’s commitment to clean sport. He said, “India firmly believes that sporting excellence must always be accompanied by integrity. Every athlete deserves a fair opportunity to compete, with success determined by talent, preparation and hard work, and not by prohibited substances or methods. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has regularly emphasised clean sport and the need to practice zero tolerance towards the menace of doping.” The Union Sports Minister highlighted the strengthening of India’s anti-doping framework through the National Anti-Doping Act, 2022, and its 2025 Amendment. “India has strengthened its legal and institutional framework through the National Anti-Doping Act, 2022, and its 2025 Amendment, both of which came into force in July 2026,” said Dr. Mandaviya. “We will also bring another amendment in the next session of our parliament, which aims to introduce criminal provisions to deal with violations even more effectively, including those by coaches and supply chain stakeholders,” he said. The Union Sports Minister further highlighted the steps India has already taken to tackle doping and inform its athletes about banned substances. “During 2025-26, the National Anti-Doping Agency of India conducted over 7,000 tests and more than 350 education and awareness sessions, reaching 27,000 participants, while focusing on risk-based testing and intelligence-led investigations,” said Dr. Mandaviya. “The Know Your Medicine mobile application has recorded over half a million searches, supporting informed decisions about medicines,” he said. Mandaviya highlighted the forthcoming signing of a Memorandum of Understanding between the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, the Ministry of Education, and UNESCO to introduce the Sport Values in Every Classroom Toolkit in India. The initiative aims to bring sporting values, ethics and integrity to classrooms and reach millions of young minds. The meeting aimed to advance global collaboration in the fight against doping and strengthen the Convention’s implementation. Discussions focused on a framework document outlining the roles and responsibilities of public authorities in the global anti-doping ecosystem, as well as strengthening anti-doping education capacity and academic research through engagement with States Parties via the National Compliance Platform. The agenda also covered resource mobilisation, the Fund’s Operational Strategy for 2026-2031, compliance and capacity-building to support a sustainable global anti-doping system. national_raw_news.title: Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 To Be Held At Dilli Haat, New Delhi, From November 1 To 15
national_raw_news.content: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 To Be Held At Dilli Haat, New Delhi, From November 1 To 15 ‘प्रकाश और परंपरा – ज्योति से ज्योति जलाएँ’ To Celebrate India’s Traditional Crafts, Festive Lighting And Cultural Heritage Showcasing Artisan Products, Traditional Craftsmanship and Cultural Programmes through Seven Thematic Zones Posted On: 27 OCT 2026 5:18PM by PIB Delhi The fortnight long Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 will be organized at Dilli Haat, INA, in the National Capital, from November 1 to 15, 2026. The Mela is being organized by the Union Ministry of Social Justice And Empowerment. Themed ‘प्रकाश और परंपरा – ज्योति से ज्योति जलाएँ’, the event will celebrate India’s traditional crafts, festive lighting and cultural heritage through artisan products, live craft demonstrations and cultural programmes. A Senior Official in the Ministry said the Mela continues the Ministry’s efforts to provide aspirational groups and communities with a platform to showcase their creativity, talent and traditional craftsmanship, while creating opportunities to market their products to a wider audience. He said since 2022, the Shilp Samagam Melas have benefited more than 1,000 artisans. The Official said this year, the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment (DoSJE) and the Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (Divyangjan) (DEPwD) will organise Shilp Utsav together for the first time, with approximately 150 stalls under Bharat TULIP and Purple Fest. The collaboration will bring together traditional artisans, creative talent and inclusive participation in a shared platform. The Ministry Official said the Mela will be curated around seven thematic zones showcasing India’s crafts, traditions, food and cultural expressions. कला आँगन will feature live craft demonstrations; प्रकाश चौक will showcase lamps and lights; पूजा पथ will present devotional products; सजावट बाज़ार will focus on home décor; घराना will feature textiles and fashion; स्वाद चौक will offer food; and मंच will host cultural activities and performances. The Official further said that Bharat TULIP (Traditional Artisans’ Upliftment Livelihood Programme) is an initiative aimed at marketing products made by aspirational groups to consumers in India and abroad through e-commerce platforms. The programme seeks to support economic empowerment while contributing to the preservation of India’s traditional arts and crafts, he added. The Ministry Official said the Purple Fest is a multidimensional celebration of disability, creativity, talent and equal participation. It brings together persons with disabilities, organisations, institutions, businesses, artists, professionals and other stakeholders to celebrate achievements, encourage participation and promote greater understanding of inclusion, he further said. Through Shilp Samagam Mela 2026, the Ministry seeks to provide greater visibility to traditional artisans and their products while celebrating India’s rich cultural heritage and encouraging wider public engagement with craftsmanship, creativity and inclusive participation. national_raw_news.title: Under Secretary assesses progress of Special Campaign 6.0 at vital Orgs under MoI&B
national_raw_news.content: Echo Of Arunachal Newsflash State News Under Secretary assesses progress of Special Campaign 6.0 at vital Orgs under MoI&B ITANAGAR, Oct 26: Shivram Meena, Under Secretary (BP&L), Ministry of Information and Broadcasting (MoI&B), Government of India, visited Akashvani, Doordarshan Kendra (DDK), the Central Bureau of Communication (CBC), the Press Information Bureau (PIB) and the Film and Television Institute of India (FTII), Itanagar today to review the progress of Special Campaign 6.0. During the visit, Meena interacted with officers and staff members and reviewed the initiatives undertaken by the respective offices under the campaign. The review focused on cleanliness and upkeep of office premises, management and disposal of e-waste, record management, optimal utilisation of office space and measures to improve administrative efficiency. He emphasised the importance of maintaining cleanliness in the workplace and sustaining the initiatives undertaken as part of the campaign. At Akashvani (Itanagar), the MoI&B official visited the campus and interacted with officers and staff members to review the initiatives undertaken under Special Campaign 6.0. He took stock of the cleanliness and upkeep of the premises, office management practices, record maintenance and utilisation of available infrastructure. During the visit, he also participated in a brief plantation activity, highlighting the importance of environmental conservation and maintaining green surroundings. At DDK, Meena inspected the studios, administrative offices, news and programme sections, record-keeping systems and other facilities. He also assessed the upkeep of the campus, interacted with officers and staff members, and stressed the need to maintain a clean and orderly working environment. He subsequently visited the CBC and the PIB, Regional Office, Itanagar, and reviewed the cleanliness and upkeep of the offices and the progress of activities undertaken under Special Campaign 6.0. He interacted with officials and staff members and took stock of the measures adopted for effective office management, record maintenance and e-waste disposal. Meena also visited the FTII, Itanagar, and reviewed the cleanliness and upkeep of the campus and the initiatives undertaken as part of Special Campaign 6.0. The Registrar and faculty members of FTII, Itanagar, accompanied him during the visit. He interacted with them and discussed measures relating to cleanliness, efficient utilisation of institutional infrastructure, record management and the maintenance of a clean and organised working environment. Utsav Parmar, Joint Director, Doordarshan and Akashvani, Itanagar; Ranjan Karmarkar, Assistant Director (E) and Head of Office, Akashvani, Itanagar; and Akhilesh Kumar Dwivedi, Assistant Director (E) and Head of Office, Doordarshan Kendra, accompanied Meena during the visit. national_raw_news.title: Department of Telecommunications records notable achievements against campaign targets
national_raw_news.content: Ministry of Communications Special Campaign 6: Department of Telecommunications records notable achievements against campaign targets Posted On: 27 OCT 2026 4:04PM by PIB Delhi As Special Campaign 6 enters its final week, the Department of Telecommunications (DoT) along with its PSUs/Subordinate offices/Attached Offices/ Autonomous Bodies/ Other Institutions has recorded notable achievements, meeting or exceeding targets in key areas of public grievance redressal, revenue generation and space management. The Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances, Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions has allocated 26.10.26 as the dedicated day for carrying out cleanliness activities across pan India offices of the Department of Telecommunications. On this dedicated day, a special drive was carried out to de-clutter office space and plantation of trees across 520 campaign sites in the Department. The Department has achieved its target for disposal of public grievances, resolving 2,270 grievances. In addition, all 640 pending public grievance appeals reported on the campaign dashboard have been disposed of. The target set for disposal of IMC references has also been fully achieved. The Department has generated Revenue of ₹2.08 crore through scrap disposal and revenue of ₹2.18 crore from e-waste disposal. The Department has so far freed 80,724 square feet of office space against a target of 45,000 square feet. These results reflect concerted efforts towards efficient record management, responsible disposal of scrap and e-waste, and better utilization of office space. Photographs of the activities carried out in field offices: Tree Plantation at C-DOT Waste to Wealth-Art Exhibition at O/o CCA, Haryana Before After Cleaning of office space at TCIL Office Space Management at BSNL Chennai Circle: Before After Clearing of office space and Tree Plantation at Gujarat LSA: Under the cleanliness drive, 520 cleanliness sites have been covered as on 26 October 2026. The campaign is continuing, with further activities planned during the remaining period. The Department of Telecommunications remains committed to sustaining the momentum of Special Campaign 6 and pursuing the campaign’s objectives during the remaining days.
